title: Sampling Distributions and Standard Error
learning_objectives: Simulate the sampling distribution of the mean with a seeded generator
Compute the standard error s / √n and explain how it shrinks with n
Describe what the central limit theorem does and does not promise
entry_point: sample_means(population, n, reps, seed); standard_error(sample); mean_ci95(sample)
hints: Create the generator once, outside the repetitions loop, so each repetition continues the stream.
Sample variance: `sum((x - m) ** 2 for x in sample) / (n - 1)`; SE is `sqrt(var) / sqrt(n)`.
`z = NormalDist().inv_cdf(0.975)`; return `(m - z * se, m + z * se)`.

failure_feedback.advice: Create one `random.Random(seed)` and draw indices with `int(rng.random() * len(population))`, n per repetition.
Each repetition must draw n values with replacement and record their mean.
Use the n - 1 sample standard deviation divided by sqrt(n).
Use `NormalDist().inv_cdf(0.975)` (≈ 1.96) times the standard error on both sides of the mean.
